title: the WSG finding water and Table 34 slice - the water-finding checks and Table 34: chance of finding water, printed p. 58 with the mechanics and the grid on p. 59
audit_label: R467 WSG finding water pin audit
audit_comment: The Table 34 grid value by value (the find% and the taint% per climate band per terrain per season, including the constant arctic rows and the human-verified tropical swamp spring cell), the two-checks-per-day rule with the auto-fail gate, the obvious-water exceptions (the snow and ice rules, the seacoast dig with its tide-line and depth gates) and the water-quality guidelines - every cell, const and bool verified against the model.

banner.title: R467: the WSG FINDING WATER slice - the water-finding checks (two per day, extra searches automatically fail, the table not used where water is obviously and readily available), the snow-and-ice exception (water for the taking if the party can melt it, the figures assume no snow or ice cover, ice at 30 degrees or lower with the taint read from the table, freshly fallen snow the purest water in nature), the nearby-fresh-water and seacoast notes (the dig-to-the-water-table 100% above the high tide line and no more than two feet deep, the deeper the saltier) and Table 34: the chance of finding water grid by climate, terrain and season, printed p. 58 with the grid on p. 59.
banner.provenance: Ground truth four-way, a NEW WORKFLOW (the user decision this round): the user ran tesseract ON TERMUX over the pdfimages-extracted scan of printed p. 59 (poppler pdfimages -f 60, TSV output with word bounding boxes), and the grid was REBUILT FROM GEOMETRY - the terrain-code column at x 130-165, the season cells at x 190/285/385/480, one row per 20 pixels of y - instead of trusting any reader reading order. The tesseract reads cross-check against the pdfy embedded OCR layer and the djvu word layer: all three agree on every one of the 224 values. The slash-loss cells (tesseract 570, 5170, 60740, 30730, 70170) all resolve to the obvious xx/yy splits confirmed by the other two readers. The low-confidence terrain labels (subarctic E, temperate =%) resolve to F (forest) - vision confirmed, and forest is the missing terrain in both bands. The ONE contested value: Tropical swamp Spring reads 90/75 in BOTH text layers (tesseract conf 40, djvu 90/75, pdfy 90/75) but 90/80 in two vision reads; the USER READ THE PHYSICAL PAGE and settled it: 90/75 - the only taint value in the whole table not ending in 0, pinned as printed. The arctic rows are constant across all four seasons; the swamp rows carry the highest find chances; the desert rows the lowest. The seacoast and snow mechanics come from the same tesseract pass (the p59_full --psm 4 text) and the printed p. 58 intro from the pdfy layer, cross-checked against the user p58 tesseract run. The where-water-is-found section (the DM standing-water reduction and the water-table definition) stays in the p. 59 gap - NOT flipped this round.
banner.sentinel: All 224 Table 34 values pinned (the find% and the taint% per climate per terrain per season); the water-finding mechanics are audit examples, including the human-verified Tropical swamp 90/75 cell and the arctic constant rows.

consts.name: wfwRowCount
consts.comment: the Table 34 row count: five climate bands x the terrain rows (arctic has no forest row; the other four climates run D/F/H/M/P/Sw)

consts.name: wfwChecksPerDay
consts.comment: a single character or a group traveling together can make two water-finding checks per day

consts.name: wfwSeacoastDigPct
consts.comment: in any seacoast area the chance of finding drinkable water by digging down to the water table is 100%

consts.name: wfwSeacoastDigMaxFt
consts.comment: the seacoast dig hole must be no more than two feet deep for the 100% chance to hold

consts.name: wfwIceTempGate
consts.comment: if the actual temperature is 30 degrees or lower, any water found in an area with no snow or ice cover will be in the form of ice

bools.name: wfwExtraSearchAutoFail
bools.comment: searches conducted more often than two per day automatically fail

bools.name: wfwNotUsedWhenObvious
bools.comment: the table should not be used in any circumstances where water is obviously and readily available

bools.name: wfwNearbyFreshWaterTaintCheck
bools.comment: characters on the bank or shore of fresh water still use the table for the taint chance unless the water is known pure and drinkable

bools.name: wfwSeaWaterDehydrates
bools.comment: drinking sea water actually dehydrates the character: the salt increases the body need for water, in large quantities or over a long period

bools.name: wfwSeacoastDigAboveTide
bools.comment: the seacoast dig hole must be dug above the high tide line for the 100% chance to hold

bools.name: wfwDigDeeperSaltier
bools.comment: the deeper one digs toward the seacoast water table, the saltier the water; digging too deep in one hole recovers water as undrinkable as the sea, though the loose soil filters out most of the salt near the surface

bools.name: wfwRiverPurerUpstream
bools.comment: river water is more likely pure closer to the source than downstream

bools.name: wfwLakePurerAtInflow
bools.comment: lake water is more likely pure where a river flows in than along the opposite shoreline where the water stagnates

bools.name: wfwFastFlowPurer
bools.comment: fast-flowing water is generally more pure than standing water

bools.name: wfwGroundWaterPurer
bools.comment: ground water, found by digging beneath the surface, is usually more pure than water found above the ground

bools.name: wfwSnowIceCoverFreeWater
bools.comment: with snow or ice cover the water is there for the taking as long as characters are willing and able to melt the snow or ice

bools.name: wfwTableAssumesNoSnowIce
bools.comment: the Table 34 figures assume that no snow or ice cover exists

bools.name: wfwIceTaintPerTable
bools.comment: ice is no more free of foreign substances than the water it formed from: the percentage chance of tainted ice is taken from the table as if water had been found

bools.name: wfwFreshSnowPurest
bools.comment: freshly fallen snow is the purest form of water available in nature; melted snow satisfies the water need as long as enough snow is available - a mere dusting provides little liquid

prev_record: - R466 LANDED 2026-10-15: commit e04918e (census 391, pushed
27481c0..e04918e), the WSG CONSUMING AND CARRYING FOOD slice, printed p. 58
- the ration ladder (one fish half a ration, one size S animal a full
ration, one size M animal feeding three characters for a day, one size L
animal six rations, at least twenty full rations from a size L carcass with
a full day of expert butchering), the druid strong disapproval of
intentional overkill with the feed-three excuse, the carry rule (excess need
not be left behind; encumbrance is a DM ruling, spoilage the other factor),
the gluttony/indigestion not-modeled note and Table 33: chance of food
spoilage (the 4x10 grid: max days before the first check then the pct chance
per subsequent day, per food type per effective-temperature band - green
plants dash/6-20/4-30/2-40/1-50, fruits or vegetables
dash/2-50/1-70/1-80/1-90), with the mechanics: the warmest category applying
at least one hour is the effective temperature, a category once used
ratchets to the same or warmer for all later checks, continually frozen food
keeps indefinitely, thawed food spoils from the thaw day (counted as day 1)
even if promptly re-frozen; one failed check taints (secret Wisdom Check to
notice, eatable anyway, CON check +4 to avoid nausea and cramps within
1d10+10 minutes - the 11-20 onset window, -1 on attacks and
dodging/maneuvering saves for 12 hours, then an unmodified CON check per
hour to recover, tainted food still a full ration); a second failed check
obviously spoils (CON check +10, penalties at least 24 hours if stricken,
else a 50% chance of the full or half ration value, otherwise no nourishment
at all). rules/wsgcarry.h NEW (47 inlines: 20 consts + 17 bools + 10 table
columns, prefix wcc - wfs was taken by R465; checked free in all three TUs).
GROUND TRUTH - the table rounds hit a new reader: the printed p. 58 image
shows scanner DOUBLE-IMAGING (a ghost copy about 12 pixels below the true
print), which is why the ASCII/pixel reads were ambiguous and the vision
calls garbage; the pdfy EMBEDDED OCR TEXT LAYER (decompress the FlateDecode
content stream of the page object and regex the Tm/Td/Tj tokens) is a
high-quality positioned text source that settles the table WITHOUT pixels -
use it (with the djvu word layer as the second reader and the arithmetic
ladders as the tiebreaker) before fighting double-imaged pixels again. Both
layers agree on every Table 33 value cell EXCEPT green-plants 31-50 (pdfy
6/20 vs a djvu garble; 6/20 fits the days ladder 6,4,2,1 and the pct ladder
20,30,40,50). The below-30 column is a dash in every row (both layers garble
the dash glyph; the book explanation sentence - spoilage will not occur as
long as the effective temperature remains within this range - confirms it);
the dash is encoded as days=0/pct=0 with the wccDashNoSpoilage bool carrying
the semantics. Note: the byte-level open_url fetch TRUNCATES around 24-32KB,
